title: Agenda
text: Alaiedon Township Planning Commission Meeting Public Hearing Monday, September 21, 2026 - 7:00 PM AGENDA Call to order and Roll Call. Approval of June 24, 2026 Planning Commission Minutes. Approval of Agenda. Correspondence. None Old Business. None New Business. a. Discussion of Drafted Ordinance Amendments: Kayla Mauldin will present drafted amendments to the Alaiedon Township Zoning Ordinance, focused on ordinance administration and application review procedures. The proposed amendments affect: • Article 1 – Title and Purpose • Article 2 – General Administration, Enforcement, and Penalties • Article 11 – Nonconforming Lots, Structures, and Uses • Article 12 – Temporary Uses (NEW ARTICLE PROPOSED) • Article 13 – Development Impact Statements (NEW ARTICLE PROPOSED) • Article 14 – Site Plan Review • Article 15 – Special Land Uses • Article 16 – Zoning Board of Appeals • Article 17 – Zoning Map and Text Amendments • Article 18 – Site Condominiums (NEW ARTICLE PROPOSED) • Article 22 – Interpretation, Severability, Vested Right, Repeal, and Effective Date. Following the presentation, the Planning Commission may ask questions and direct further revisions to the drafted ordinances. The discussion will cover Phase I of Alaiedon Township's Zoning Ordinance Update project. At future meetings, the Commission will discuss proposed amendments to zoning districts, use standards, and site development standards. A public hearing on all proposed amendments to the Zoning Ordinance will be held later in 2027. Public Comments. Public will be allowed to address the Planning Commission one (1) time only with a time limit of three (3) minutes. Public comment is not a question-and-answer period. Adjourn.

text: Supervisor Fonda J. Brewer Clerk Mary R. Clark Treasurer Dennis R. Fedewa Manager Brian T. Reed Trustee Elizabeth S. Bowen Trustee Andrea M. Cascarilla Trustee Karen J. Mojica Trustee Joshua I. Delta Zoom is also inviting interested individuals to attend via the scheduled Zoom meeting. CHARTER TOWNSHIP OF DELTA PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES: September 14, 2026 I. CALL TO ORDER Chair Kosinski called the meeting to order at 6:00 P.M. II. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE III. ROLL CALL IV. Members Present: Chair Kosinski, Vice-Chair Hunt-Proctor, Secretary Weldon, Mudry, Howell, Meddaugh, McConnell, Bradley Members Absent: None Others Present: Director of Planning & Economic Development Peter Menser, Associate Planner Hope Wojack, Associate Planner Hayden James, Planning Department Assistant Sarah Anderton APPROVAL OF AGENDA Commissioner Mudry made a motion that the agenda be approved as submitted. Commissioner Hunt-Proctor supported the motion. VOICE VOTE. Carried 8-0. V. APPROVAL OF MINUTES • Minutes of August 24, 2026 regular meeting Commissioner Hunt-Proctor made a motion that the minutes from August 24, 2026 be approved as submitted. Commissioner Mudry supported the motion. VOICE VOTE. Carried 8-0. VI. CORRESPONDENCE – None VII. OLD BUSINESS – None VIII. PUBLIC HEARING A. Rezoning #PRZ2026-0002 (Eyde Development): Rezone 53.98 acres located on the east side of S. Marketplace Blvd., north of W. St. Joseph Hwy., comprised of the entirety of Parcel #040-016-400 220-00 and a portion of Parcel #040-016-300-148-02 as 8158 Executive Ct.) from O (Office) and AG2 (addressed (Agricultural/Residential) to RM (Multiple Family) with a condition voluntarily offered by the applicant to limit development on the project site to a maximum of 480 dwelling units. Commissioner Hunt-Proctor made a motion to open the public hearing. Commissioner McConnell supported the motion. AGENDA CHARTER TOWNSHIP OF DELTA PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES: SEPTEMBER 14, 2026 VOICE VOTE. Carried 8-0. Director Menser introduced the rezoning request from Eye Development. Topics of note included: • Eyde Development has voluntarily offered to condition the requested rezoning on limiting development in the area proposed for rezoning to a maximum of 480 dwelling units. • The area currently has public utilities (water and sewer) available. • The applicant has recently delineated the wetlands in the area. Mark Clouse, Eyde Development, 300 S Washington Square, Suite 400, Lansing, MI 48933: Mr. Clouse introduced himself and described the rezoning request. Nathaniel Eyde, Eyde Development, 300 S Washington Square, Suite 400, Lansing, MI 48933: Mr. Eyde addressed questions about whether they would provide affordable housing. He said they must weigh the cost of building with the rent they can afford to charge. Chair Kosinski closed the public hearing. Commissioner McConnell made a motion: “I move that the Planning Commission recommend to the Delta Township Board of Trustees approval of the request to rezone 53.98 acres located on the east side of S. Marketplace Blvd., north of W. St. Joseph Hwy., comprised of the entirety of Parcel #040-016-400-220-00 and a portion of Parcel #040-016-300-148 02 from O (Office) and AG2 (Agricultural/Residential) to RM (Multiple Family) with a condition voluntarily offered by the applicant to limit development on the project site to a maximum of 480 dwelling units. for the following reasons: 1. The proposed rezoning request meets the criteria specified for rezoning in Section 16.04 (Criteria for Amendment to the Official Zoning Map) of the Delta Township Zoning Ordinance. 2. The subject site meets the minimum standards for lot area and lot width of the proposed RM zoning district. 3. The proposed rezoning addresses the Township Board goal of encouraging a diverse population by establishing a new area for potential multiple-family residential development. 4. The proposed rezoning aligns with the designation of Mixed Use and Multi-family residential on the Future Land Use Map from the 2026 Master Plan. 5. Public water and sanitary sewer are available to serve the site.” Commissioner Hunt-Proctor supported the motion. ROLL CALL VOTE. Carried 7-1 (Dissenting: Commissioner Howell) Staff advised applicants on the next steps. 2 CHARTER TOWNSHIP OF DELTA PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES: SEPTEMBER 14, 2026 B. Proposed Zoning Amendment (Berroa): Request to amend Section 8.47(a) of the Zoning Ordinance to remove the requirement that primary parcel access for all nonpublic schools shall be on a county primary road, as classified by the Eaton County Road Commission, or on a state trunk line under the jurisdiction of the Michigan Department of Transportation. Chair Kosinski opened the public hearing. Associate Planner James introduced the proposed zoning amendment. He explained that a zoning amendment can be initiated by the Township Board or Planning Commission, or a resident can apply for it. This proposed zoning amendment would revise Section 8.47(a) of the Delta Township Zoning Ordinance to exempt nonpublic schools from the requirement to have primary road access. The applicant is Nicholas Berroa, on behalf of Cedar Classical Academy. The school is currently located at 7520 Westshire Drive and is considering moving to 1044 Eastbury Drive to accommodate their growing student population. 7520 Westshire Drive, the school’s current location since November 2023, is not on a county primary road. When the school originally moved to this location, they were directed by Planning staff to seek a variance from the primary road requirement from the Zoning Board of Appeals (ZBA). This request was considered by the ZBA on January 6, 2023, which ultimately voted to approve the variance. However, the intent of the ZBA is to consider spatial, dimensional variances. Because the requirement for county primary road access is public policy rather than a dimensional standard, it was incorrect to refer the applicant to the ZBA. Recognizing this error, Planning staff informed the applicant that a zoning amendment would be the best option. Nicholas Berroa, applicant, 7116 Willow Woods Circle, Lansing, MI 48917: Mr. Berroa introduced himself and explained his reasons for the zoning amendment request. He said that Cedar Classical Academy does not use buses, as most private schools do not so traffic should not be a concern. He included that many families have multiple children that are being driven in a single vehicle. He added that there are currently 136 students and they are near capacity in the current location. Mr. Berroa shared an example of larger cities that allow private schools to be on a nonprimary road, citing Jackson and Kalamazoo. Commissioners discussed the following topics: • Concerns about changing the broader zoning requirements • Concern about emergency vehicle access • Question about the composition of private roads • The agency responsible for snow plowing public roads • Whether or not the amendment should include both public and nonpublic schools Caroline Hummel, Director of Advancement, Cedar Classical Academy, 7520 Westshire Drive, Lansing, MI 48917: Ms. Hummel explained the school and its development. 3 CHARTER TOWNSHIP OF DELTA PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES: SEPTEMBER 14, 2026 Commissioner McConnell made a motion to close the public hearing. Commissioner Meddaugh supported the motion. VOICE VOTE. Carried 8-0. Commissioner Bradley made a motion: “I move to recommend approval of the requested amendment to Section 8.47(a) of the Zoning Ordinance to exempt nonpublic schools from the requirement to be located on a county primary road or state trunk line.” Commissioner Mudry supported the motion. • AMENDMENT #1 OF ORIGINAL MOTION. Commissioner Weldon made a motion to amend the original motion to add public schools in addition to nonpublic. Commissioner Weldon made an amended motion: “I move to recommend approval of the requested amendment to Section 8.47(a) of the Zoning Ordinance to exempt public and nonpublic schools from the requirement to be located on a county primary road or state trunk line.” Commissioner McConnell supported the motion. • AMENDMENT #2 OF PREVIOUS MOTION. Commissioner Howell made motion to amend the first amended motion to add “as long as it is a road maintained by the Eaton County Road Commission.” Commissioner Howell made an amended motion: “I move to recommend approval of the requested amendment to Section 8.47(a) of the Zoning Ordinance to exempt public and nonpublic schools from the requirement to be located on a county primary road or state trunk line as long as it is a road maintained by the Eaton County Road Commission.” Commissioner McConnell supported the motion. • REVISED AMENDMENT #3 OF PREVIOUS MOTION. Commissioner Howell made another motion to revise the second amendment to remove “maintained by the Eaton County Road Commission” and add “as long as it is a public road.” Commissioner Howell made an amended motion: “I move to recommend approval of the requested amendment to Section 8.47(a) of the Zoning Ordinance to exempt nonpublic and public schools from the requirement to be located on a county primary road or state trunk line as long as it is a public road.” Commissioner Weldon supported the motion. 4 CHARTER TOWNSHIP OF DELTA PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES: SEPTEMBER 14, 2026 • Commissioner Howell made an amended motion: I move to recommend approval of the requested amendment to Section 8.47(a) of the Zoning Ordinance to exempt nonpublic schools from the requirement to be located on a county primary road or state trunk line as long as it is a public road. Commissioner McConnell previously supported the motion. ROLL CALL VOTE Carried 6-2. (Dissenting: Commissioners Bradley and Hunt-Proctor) • Commissioner Weldon made a motion: “I move to recommend approval of the requested amendment to Section 8.47(a) of the Zoning Ordinance to exempt nonpublic and public schools from the requirement to be located on a county primary road or state trunk line.” Commissioner McConnell previously supported the motion. ROLL CALL VOTE Failed 4-4. (Dissenting: Commissioners Bradley, Hunt-Proctor, Meddaugh and Mudry) • Commissioner Howell made a motion: “I move to recommend approval of the requested amendment to Section 8.47(a) of the Zoning Ordinance to exempt nonpublic or public schools from the requirement to be located on a county primary road or state trunk line as long as it is a public road.” Commissioner Weldon previously supported the motion. ROLL CALL VOTE Failed 3-5. (Dissenting: Commissioners Bradley, Hunt-Proctor, Meddaugh, McConnell and Weldon) MOTION FAILED TO CARRY. Commissioners continued to discuss whether the wording of the amendment could be reworked. Director Menser reiterated that this policy amendment cannot go through the ZBA as they look at dimensional variances only per state law, nor can the ZBA amend its zoning code language to allow these types of requests. The Township Board can now approve it, deny it, or send it back to the Planning Commission for reconsideration. IX. OTHER BUSINESS – None X. PUBLIC COMMENTS – None 5 CHARTER TOWNSHIP OF DELTA PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES: SEPTEMBER 14, 2026 XI. PLANNING DIRECTOR COMMENTS The next meeting on September 28, will have one public hearing – a Special Land Use Permit for a Kroger Pharmacy drive-through at 6430 W. Saginaw Hwy. XII. PLANNING COMMISSIONER COMMENTS – None XIII. ADJOURNMENT Chair Kosinski adjourned the meeting at 7:58 P.M Respectfully Submitted, ___ Secretary Bob Weldon 6 Supervisor Fonda J. Brewer Clerk Mary R. Lyman Planning Department (517) 323-8560 To: Delta Township Planning Commission From: Hope Wojack, Associate Planner Date: September 21, 2026 Subject: Special Land Use Permit #PSL2026-0003 (Kroger Pharmacy Drive-Through), add a new drive-through pharmacy lane and pharmacy window to the west side of the existing building located at 6430 W. Saginaw Hwy. (Parcel #040-010-400-111-00). Matt Andrus of Jeffery A Scott Architects P.C., on behalf of client The Kroger Company of Michigan, is seeking Special Land Use Permit (SLUP) approval to add a new drive-through pharmacy lane and pharmacy window to the west side of the existing building located at 6430 W. Saginaw Hwy. (Parcel #040-010-400-111-00). The subject parcel is 9.15 acres in size and zoned C (Commercial). The building was constructed in 1992 and is 76,674 square feet in size. This Kroger location already has a pharmacy located inside the store in the vicinity of the proposed drive-through window and lane. SLUP Process The Special Land Use Permit process consists of two phases, a public hearing at the Planning Commission followed by review of the project by the Delta Township Board. For SLUP, the Planning Commission is advisory to the Board. It will provide a recommendation on the request, with the Board granting final approval. If SLUP approval is granted by the Township Board, the project still must receive Site Plan Review approval prior to moving ahead to building and trades permit applications. Surrounding Zoning and Land Uses North: RC - Moderate Density Residential (Bickford Assisted Living & Memory Care) South: C - Commercial (W. Saginaw Hwy/Champion Chrysler, Miller Animal Clinic, Walgreens) South: O - Office (PNC Bank) East: RB - Low Density Residential (Creyts Rd/Single Family Residential) West: C - Commercial (Red Robin, Kohl’s) The following provides a summary of the proposal’s consistency with the special land use permit criteria and the specific ordinance standards for a restaurant with drive-through. SLUP Standards of Approval (Section 7.03) 1. Compatibility with the Comprehensive Plan. The proposed Special Land Use shall be compatible and in accordance with the goals, objectives and policies of the Delta Charter Township Comprehensive Plan and any associated sub-area and corridor plans. AGENDA MOTION Kroger Pharmacy Drive-Through (6430 W. Saginaw Hwy) SLUP Planning Commission (September 28, 2026) Page 2 Staff comment: The proposed project aligns with the 2026 Master Plan and the Future Land Use Map designation of Commercial zoning. 2. Compatibility with Adjacent Uses. The proposed Special Land Use shall be constructed, operated, and maintained so as to be compatible with the existing or intended character of the general vicinity and so as not to change the essential character of the area in which it is proposed. A Special Land Use shall be designed and constructed so as not to create a significant detrimental impact, as compared to the impacts of permitted uses. Staff comment: The subject property is located at the intersection of W. Saginaw Hwy. and Creyts Rd. within the Commercial zoning district. The proposed drive-through lane would be located on the west side of the existing building, within the interior of the parcel. The surrounding area is predominantly developed with commercial and office uses. Additionally, the proposed drive-through is adequately buffered from surrounding properties. Given the existing development pattern and proposed location of the drive-through, the use is not anticipated to have a detrimental impact on surrounding residential properties. 3. Impact on Public Services. The proposed Special Land Use shall be served adequately by essential public facilities and services, such as highways, streets, police and fire protection, drainage, water and sewage facilities. Such services shall be provided and accommodated without an unreasonable public burden. Staff comment: The existing store and pharmacy are already served by public facilities and services; the proposed drive-through will not impact these items. 4. Impact on the Overall Environment. The proposed Special Land Use shall not involve uses, activities, processes, materials and equipment, or conditions of operation that will be detrimental to the natural environment, public health, safety, or welfare by reason of excessive production of traffic, noise, smoke, odors, or other such nuisance in comparison to the impacts associated with typical permitted uses. Staff comment: There is no additional impact on the overall environment anticipated due to the building already being present on the parcel. The pharmacy drive-through lane will not alter any of the existing site characteristics. 5. Traffic Impact. The proposed Special Land Use shall be located and designed in a manner which will minimize the impact of traffic, taking into consideration: pedestrian access and safety; vehicle trip generation (i.e. volumes); types of traffic, access location and design, circulation and parking design; street and bridge capacity; and traffic operations at nearby intersections and access points. Efforts shall be made to ensure that multiple transportation modes are safely and effectively accommodated to provide alternate modes of access and alleviate vehicular traffic congestion. The applicant shall comply with the Township Complete Street Ordinance. Staff comment: A traffic study was not required for this SLUP because the pharmacy that the drive-through will serve already exists. The addition of a drive-through is not anticipated to increase traffic to the location. The applicant has stated that the parking lot will remain the same. 6. Operational Characteristics. The nature and character of the activities, processes, materials, equipment, or conditions of operation, either specifically or typically associated with the use shall be reviewed. Staff comment: Negative impacts are not anticipated from the construction of the new drive-through lanes. Kroger Pharmacy Drive-Through (6430 W. Saginaw Hwy) SLUP Planning Commission (September 28, 2026) Page 3 7. Outdoor Operations. Measures shall be taken to ensure that outdoor activity, storage, and work areas will be compatible with adjacent land uses. Staff comment: The new outdoor operations will be located in the interior of the lot, adjacent to the neighboring commercial property parking lot, making it compatible with neighboring land uses. 8. Compliance with Zoning Ordinance Standards. The proposed Special Land Use shall be designed, constructed, operated, and maintained to meet the stated intent of the zoning district and shall comply with all applicable ordinance standards. Staff comment: The site plan provided by the applicant meets the commercial zoning standards and SLUP standards for drive-throughs. The proposed project has been designed to meet the intent of the zoning ordinance and will comply with all applicable ordinance

WHEREAS, the Charter Township of Flushing will hold a public hearing to return its general fund operating levy to .5000mills from .4828 mills, the rate rolled back by Truth in Taxation. The difference is .0172 mills or 3.56% and returns our authorized mill to .5000 mills. The Township is authorized to levy 1.0400 mills. WHEREAS, the Township proposes to levy 3.1456 mills on the authorized 3.4114 mills approved for police operations. The present rate of 3.0628 mills, as rolled back by Truth in Taxation, if returned to 3.1456 mills will represent a change of 2.7% or .0828 mills. IT IS RESOLVED: 1. 2. 3. 4. Seymour Road, Flushing, Michigan as part of the special meeting of the Charter Township of Flushing Board of Trustees. Notice of the public hearing, in the form attached to this Resolution was posted at the Township offices and published in an appropriate newspaper at least 6 days prior to the public hearing in accordance with MCL211.24e(6). The general fund operating millage is returned to .5000 mills and the police operations millage is returned to 3.1456 mills and the respective millage shall be levied at the returned rates. Invocation Supervisor Spicher led the invocation for the Board and the members of the public. Pledge of Allegiance The Pledge of Allegiance was recited. Roll Call The following members were present constituting a quorum for the transaction of business: Kevin Spicher, Candie Hovarter, Robin Hunt, Bill Reiber, Rick Soucy, Jodi Valenti, and Todd Walker. Also present was Township Manager Kelly VanMarter, Township Attorney Kali Henderson, and five people in the audience. Call to the Public The call to the public was opened at 6:32 pm with no response. Approval of Consent Agenda: Moved by Soucy, supported by Valenti, to approve the Consent Agenda with item #2 only. The motion carried unanimously. 1. Payment of Bills: September 8, 2026 (moved to Regular Agenda) 2. Request to approve the August 17, 2026 regular meeting minutes. Approval of Regular Agenda: Moved by Reiber, supported by Walker, to approve the Regular Agenda with Payment of Bills: September 8, 2026 added. The motion carried unanimously. 1. Payment of Bills: September 8, 2026 (moved from Consent Agenda) 1 Packet Page 10 Genoa Charter Township Board Meeting September 8, 2026 Unapproved Minutes Mr. Reiber questioned why the total was approximately $300,000 more than usual. Ms. VanMarter stated this amount included payments for some of the road SAD projects and election employee payments. He also questioned the flag services item. Ms. VanMarter stated the company, Rocket, provides service to the township to maintain the American, POW and Genoa Flags. This is an annual contract that was renewed. Moved by Hunt, supported by Soucy, to approve the Payment of Bills: September 8, 2026. The motion carried unanimously. 3. Consideration of a request for approval of the First Amendment to the Water Tower Lease Agreement with New Cingular Wireless PCS, LLC (formerly AT&T) for the Oak Pointe water tower located at 4500 Country Club Drive, Brighton, MI 48116. Dr. Greg Tatara stated AT&T approached the township to install additional antennas on this tower. The appropriate tests were completed and some aesthetic requests were made by MHOG and the Villas at Oak Point, who own the property where the tower is located. He showed the tower currently and what it will look like after the other antennas are installed. Dr. Tatara and the board discussed the proposed changes to the contract. Moved by Soucy, supported by Hunt, to approve the First Amendment to the Water Tower Lease Agreement with New Cingular Wireless PCS, LLC (formerly AT&T) for the Oak Pointe water tower located at 4500 Country Club Drive, Brighton, MI 48116. The motion carried unanimously. Ms. Hunt commended MHOG with getting through the storm with no interruptions in service. It shows what an excellent staff they have. Dr. Tatara agrees. His staff worked several 12 hour days in a row. There was also assistance from local businesses. 4. Consideration of a recommendation for approval of an environmental impact assessment and site plan for a proposed 6,515 sq. ft. building with 8 vehicle bays for a minor auto repair establishment in the existing Livingston Commons Phase 2 Planned Unit Development. The property is located on the south side of Grand Oaks Drive and west of S. Latson Road. The request is petitioned by Zaremba Group, LLC. A. Disposition of Environmental Impact Assessment dated June 19, 2026 B. Disposition of Site Plan dated July 14, 2026. Mr. Justin Bruce of the Zaremba Group and Ms. Whitney Pizzala of AR Engineering were present. Mr. Bruce provided a review of the project and what type of auto maintenance will be performed at this location. They showed colored renderings and building material samples. This 2 Packet Page 11 Genoa Charter Township Board Meeting September 8, 2026 Unapproved Minutes building will be leased by Firestone. He noted they take great care of the properties they lease and an average lease for them is 51 years. Mr. Reiber stated the Planning Commission gave the project a positive review. There are some minor conditions they recommended. He thanked the applicant for putting the facilities right next to a gas station which is a compatible use. Supervisor Spicher requested to have the applicant comply with the Buffer Zone C requirement. Mr. Bruce stated they will meet this requirement. Ms. Hunt requested to have a “Coming Soon…” sign put on the property once the construction begins. Mr. Bruce stated they will place a sign when they close on the property. They anticipate starting construction after the first of the year. Mr. Walker noted that there were two wall signs shown on the plans and asked for clarification as to whether or not those are allowed. Ms. VanMarter responded that this is in a PUD which may be different regulations. She recommended including in the motion a comment that the signs meet the requirements. Moved by Soucy, supported by Hunt, to approve the Environmental Impact Assessment dated June 19, 2026 for a proposed 6,515 sq. ft. building with eight vehicle bays for a minor auto repair establishment for a vacant parcel (4711-08-200-022) located on the south side of Grand Oaks Drive, west of S. Latson Road with the following condition: 1. The hours of operation shall be added to the Environmental Impact Assessment prior to land use permit issuance. The motion carried unanimously. Moved by Hunt, supported by Hovarter, to approve the site plan dated July 14, 2026 for a proposed 6,515 sq. ft. building with eight vehicle bays for a minor auto repair establishment for a vacant parcel (4711-08-200-022) located on the south side of Grand Oaks Drive, west of S. Latson Road with the following conditions: 1. The land division required for this project shall be completed prior to the issuance of a Land Use Permit. 2. The land division will include the cross-access easements required to accommodate the site plan as presented. Cross-access easements shall be recorded prior to land use permit issuance. 3. Prior to issuance of a land use permit, a concept plan depicting the proposed land division and resulting property lines shall be submitted. The concept plan shall include the two remaining parcels and identify all cross-access easements between the parcels including the two remaining parcels. The plan shall demonstrate that the proposed building and all resulting parcels comply with applicable Township Zoning Ordinance requirements, including setbacks, lot area, lot width, access, parking, and other applicable site development standards. 4. Two more parking lot trees will be established within the landscape plan. 5. The petitioner will meet all requirements of the Fire Marshal’s letter dated July 22, 2026 prior to issuance of a Land Use Permit. 3 Packet Page 12 Genoa Charter Township Board Meeting September 8, 2026 Unapproved Minutes 6. The petitioner will meet all requirements of the township engineer’s letter from August 4, 2026 prior to issuance of a Land Use Permit. 7. The petitioner will meet all requirements of the township planner’s letter dated July 31, 2026 prior to issuance of a Land Use Permit. 8. Two trees or eight shrubs shall be planted in Buffer Zone C. 9. The applicant shall comply with the township sign ordinance. The motion carried unanimously. 5. Consideration of a request for approval and adoption of Ordinance Number 260908 for the proposed revised Genoa Charter Township Peddlers and Solicitors Ordinance. (Roll Call) Supervisor Spicher stated this is a modification of the existing ordinance due to some concerns raised by Mr. Soucy. It has been reviewed and approved by Ms. Henderson. Ms. VanMarter stated that if the ordinance is passed, it must be published before it is effective. This may be delayed to allow staff to develop the Do Not Knock list software, window decals, and any associated fees. Moved by Reiber, supported by Walker, to approve and adopt Ordinance Number 260908 for the proposed revised Genoa Charter Township Peddlers and Solicitors Ordinance. The motion carried unanimously with a roll call vote (Reiber - yes; Hunt- yes; Valenti - yes; Hovarter yes; Soucy - yes; Walker - yes; Spicher - yes) 6. Consideration of a request for approval of Resolution 260908 Recognizing September 11-17 Annually as Patriot Week in Genoa Charter Township. (Roll Call) Moved by Soucy, supported by Walker, to approve Resolution 260908 Recognizing September 11- September 17 Annually as Patriot Week in Genoa Charter Township. The motion carried unanimously with a roll call vote (Hunt - yes; Valenti - yes; Hovarter - yes; Walker - yes; Reiber - yes; Soucy - yes; Spicher - yes) Items for Discussion 7. Discussion of roundabout beautification as requested by the Township Supervisor. Supervisor Spicher stated the roundabout at Bauer and Challis is unsightly. The Livingston County Road Commission will mow it twice a year so if any other maintenance is warranted, it would need to be done by Genoa Township, with approval from the Road Commission. After a brief discussion, the board agreed to pursue improvements to this roundabout and the one located at Chilson and Coon Lake Road. 4 Packet Page 13 Genoa Charter Township Board Meeting September 8, 2026 Unapproved Minutes 8. Discussion of Board Member Code of Conduct and Decorum policy as requested by the Administrative Committee. Supervisor Spicher stated there are some local municipalities that have a code of conduct. Mr. Reiber stated the current code of conduct policy was shredded during the last election period. It was an embarrassment the way some people treated other people on this board in public. Ms. Valenti asked for clarification on whether or not the Board has a policy. Ms. VanMarter stated that she believes Mr. Reiber is referencing the Principles of Governance which is not a policy. Ms. Henderson stated adding a policy such as this can add a layer of protection for the township in the case of future litigation. Mr. Walker is concerned that this policy could affect the board member’s first amendment rights. Ms. Henderson stated if the policy is written correctly, it would not. Ms. Valenti is not opposed to a policy for guidelines and education for the board members. Supervisor Spicher will research similar policies and work with the attorney to develop a policy to bring to the board. 9. Update on the Eagle Scout project at the Chilson Hills Cemetery as presented by the Township Clerk. Mr. Soucy stated eagle scout candidate, Luke O’Brian, requested to do a project at the Chilson Hills Cemetery. Luke, his family and fellow troop members spent more than 40 hours cleaning 40 headstones and repairing 3. The township will also be implementing a fall clean up event at the cemetery. Mr. Reiber congratulated Luke on earning his Eagle Scout. It is a very high honor and will be with him his entire life. Board Comments Ms. Hovarter provided a review of the Melonfest. Supervisor Spicher provided a review of the housing town hall. There were approximately 15 people in attendance. A follow up survey will be published regarding South Latson Road. Ms. Hunt stated September 14 is the last day to pay summer taxes without penalty. At this time, it is best to pay online or drop off the payment at the township or in one of the drop boxes, instead of mailing it. Adjournment 5 Packet Page 14 Genoa Charter Township Board Meeting September 8, 2026 Unapproved

Public Hearing a. Site Plan Application Site Plan with Special Land Use Application #26-006 - Request to construct a two family dwelling in the Village of Hartland (Avon Street) Chair Fox explained the process and opened the Public Hearing at 7:03 PM stating all public notice requirements have been met. Director Langer stated the following:  Gave an overview of the location and scope of the project.  Located in the Village of Hartland near the intersection of Crouse Road and Avon Street.  Zoned LI (Limited Commercial); two family dwellings units are permitted in this zoning district by Special Use Permit.  Applicant would like to construct a duplex or two family dwelling unit on vacant land located on Avon Street in the Village of Hartland.  Special Use Permit requires a public hearing with a recommendation from the Planning Commission. The application will then be heard by the Township Board for a final decision. Kelly Summerfield of Creative Design and Construction, representing the Applicant, Paul Mika, stated the Special Use of the two family dwelling is in character with the other uses in that area. They could also be used as professional offices in the future. 2 HARTLAND TOWNSHIP PLANNING COMMISSION DRAFT MEETING MINUTES SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 – 7:00 PM Chair Fox mentioned a communication was received from Carrie Jellison, CPA. Call to Public:  Gary Cornillaud, owner of 3508 Avon and past owner of the subject property; offered some corrections to the staff memorandum and expressed concern regarding grading, drainage and setbacks.  David Schneider, representing his mother’s estate at 3515 Washington; expressed similar concerns regarding grading, drainage and setbacks.  Kathryn Savla, 3546 Mill; expressed concern about increased traffic and maintaining the Village aesthetic.  Brian Schneider, former resident at 3515 Washington; feels it should be an office or business use rather than residential and concerned about the duplexes not being occupied by the property owners. Chair Fox closed the Public Hearing at 7:22 PM. Discussion Chair Fox referred to the staff review letter dated September 3, 2026. SPECIAL LAND USE REVIEW – General Standards Chair Fox mentioned the Planning Department believes the proposed use can and will meet the criteria listed for the special land use request; and the applicant has provided written responses to the special land use general standards in his email dated August 13, 2026. The Planning Commission offered no comments. SPECIAL LAND USE REVIEW – Applicable Site standards Chair Fox commented the proposed multiple family structure has two (2) dwelling units. Each dwelling unit is approximately 978 square feet in area (useable living area) and has two (2) bedrooms. Each dwelling unit complies with Section 3.24.10. for the required minimum floor area of 850 square feet. The Planning Commission offered no comments. SITE PLAN REVIEW – Applicable Site Standards Dimensional Requirements (LC- Limited Commercial; Section 3.1.12) Director Langer stated standard found in Section 3.1.12. E. states “Same as existing lots or existing building if re-use,” with no specific dimensions; thus, staff views the 0.227-acre lot size area in comparison to the surrounding properties and views it as compliant. Commissioner Mayer asked about the side setback to the south. Director Langer explained the aerial view issues with lines on the map; continued stating the site plan indicated the setback for this structure would be five (5) feet. Chair Fox stated this parcel is already in existence; it is not a newly created parcel so this standard may not apply to this situation. Director Langer concurred. Hartland Township Page 2 Updated 9/17/26 3 HARTLAND TOWNSHIP PLANNING COMMISSION DRAFT MEETING MINUTES SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 – 7:00 PM Building Setbacks (Sec. 3.1.12.E.) Director Langer reviewed the setback table. Commissioner Murphy asked the Planning Commission for their opinion on two neighbors sharing essentially one driveway approximately twenty-one (21) feet wide. The Planning Commission felt that width is standard for a duplex use and acceptable. The Planning Commission briefly discussed parking in the area. Architecture in the LC District (Sec. 3.20) Chair Fox stated the standard stated that buildings shall possess architectural variety but enhance the overall cohesiveness and historic settlement character. They are using Hardie board and batten products. The Planning Commission offered no comments. Side Setback (Sec. 3.24.11.) Director Langer stated the following:  Standard refers to how the lots abut stating “15-foot side setback where walls of structures face interior side lot lines and contain windows or other openings.”  South lot is a corner lot so the Planning Commission may or may not consider it a side yard; the Planning Commission may also decide if that is considered an interior lot line.  Also mentions windows or other openings.  Proposed on the north and south sides of each unit are sliding glass doors with patios. The Planning Commission discussed the definition of interior side lot line, how they should apply this standard, if they should use the LC Limited Commercial setbacks for this property, or if they should prohibit a sliding door or window on the north façade. Planning Commission suggested if the structure cannot be shifted south to meet the fifteen (15) foot setback on the north side and the south patio reduced in size, then the door opening on the north façade must be removed; or the Applicant can go to the Zoning Board of Appeals and seek a variance. The Applicant stated he would work with staff and discuss it with Mr. Mika. Commissioner Eckman stated the drainage is regulated by the Livingston County Drian Commissioner’s office. The Planning Commission has neither the authority nor the expertise to manage the project. Director Langer addressed the comments requesting a grading plan stating that typically a grading plan is not required for single family or duplex new construction; a site plan is required. Commissioner Mayer stated now that the Applicant is well aware of the concerns of the neighboring properties, he hopes the Applicant will address those concerns; if the neighbors have additional concerns, they should speak to the Livingston County Drain Commission. Director Langer stated this project will not be submitted to the Township Engineer as that process is for commercial projects only, not single family or duplex residential properties. If it were a Hartland Township Page 3 Updated 9/17/26 4 HARTLAND TOWNSHIP PLANNING COMMISSION DRAFT MEETING MINUTES SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 – 7:00 PM commercial project, the likelihood of runoff and increased water drainage could be greater than this use. Chair Fox stated it will have far less traffic than an office use. Director Langer concurred. Chair Fox addressed a concern for the written communication about parking stating this property can park up to six (6) vehicles; parking should not be a problem. Commissioner Grissim also mentioned residential traffic and parking occur at opposite times of the day as a commercial use. Commissioner Mitchell asked to confirm if the septic field has been removed. The Applicant stated he feels it has not as the grade is slightly raised in that location. Commissioner Mayer stated he visited the site earlier around 4:20PM and counted no less than seventeen available parking spaces at that time and does not believe parking will be an issue. Commissioner Murphy asked the Applicant to label the width of the driveway as twenty-one (21) feet. The Applicant agreed. Commissioner Eckman offered the following Motion: Move to recommend approval of Special Land Use Permit and approve Site Plan Application #26-006, proposed two family dwelling on a vacant lot on Avon Street (Tax Parcel ID #470816-101-125) as stated in the staff memorandum dated September 3, 2026. The recommendation for approval is based on the following findings: 1. The proposed special land use, two family dwelling, meets the intent and purposes of the Ordinance as well as the specific standards outlined in Section 6.6 (Special Uses). 2. The proposed special land use is permitted in the LC (Limited Commercial) zoning district, as outlined in Section 3.1.12.D.i., and the proposed use is compatible with the existing uses in the vicinity. 3. The proposed use will be served by private well (water) and municipal sanitary sewer, by existing essential facilities and public services, and the Hartland Deerfield Fire Authority has no objection. 4. The proposed multiple family structure (duplex) meets the minimum requirements for usable floor area in each dwelling unit. 5. The proposed use will not create additional requirements at public cost for public facilities as the proposed site will be served by a private well (water) and municipal sanitary sewer. Approval is subject to the following conditions: 1. The proposed special land use, two family dwelling, is subject to approval by the Township Board. Hartland Township Page 4 Updated 9/17/26 5 HARTLAND TOWNSHIP PLANNING COMMISSION DRAFT MEETING MINUTES SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 – 7:00 PM 2. The applicant shall adequately address the outstanding items noted in the Planning Department’s memorandum, September 3, 2026, on the plans submitted with a land use permit application, subject to an administrative review by the Planning staff prior to the issuance of a land use permit. 3. A land use permit is required after approval of the Site Plan and Special Land Use Permit. 4. The proposed use shall be served by municipal sanitary sewer. 5. Applicant complies with any requirements of the Department of Public Works Director, Township Engineering Consultant (SDA), Hartland Deerfield Fire Authority, and all other government agencies, as applicable. 6. If the structure cannot be shifted south to meet the fifteen (15) foot setback on the north side, then the door opening on the north façade must be removed; or the Applicant can seek a variance from the Zoning Board of Appeals. Seconded by Commissioner Grissim. Motion carried unanimously. 8. Call to the Public: None 9. Planner Report: None 10. Committee Reports: None 11. Adjournment: A Motion to adjourn was made by Commissioner Mitchell and seconded by Commissioner Murphy. Motion carried unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at approximately 8:07 PM. Hartland Township Page 5 Updated 9/17/26 6 Hartland Township Planning Commission Meeting Agenda Memorandum Submitted By: Troy Langer, Planning Director Subject: Site Plan Application #26-009 – Amended and Restated Eighth Amendment to Hartland Towne Square Planned Development Agreement Date: September 17, 2026 Recommended Action Move to recommend approval of Site Plan Application #26-009, for the Amended and Restated Eighth Amendment to Hartland Towne Square Planned Development Agreement, as outlined in the staff memorandum dated September 17, 2026. The recommendation for approval is based on the following findings: 1. The Planning Commission has determined the proposed amendment provides clarification for the ongoing maintenance of the private roads in the development. 2. The Planning Commission has determined the proposed amendment to remove the limitation on the number of drive-through establishments provides flexibility for existing and future businesses in the development. 3. The Planning Commission has determined the proposed amendments to allow additional ground signs, make improvements to existing ground signs, and amend the wall sign standards improves the visibility for existing and future businesses in the development. 4. The Planning Commission has determined the amendment to update the lighting standards to add LED light pole heads will be a benefit to the PD and the Township. 5. The Planning Commission has determined the proposed landscape modifications and enhancements to certain landscaping areas will be a benefit to the development as well as for existing and future businesses. 6. The Planning Commission has determined the proposed amendment to allow for additional permitted uses by right provides flexibility for existing and future businesses in the development. 7. The Planning Commission has determined the proposed modifications in the façade material products for the buildings will allow for flexibility for future businesses. 8. The Planning Commission has determined the proposed modifications to the building height limitations will allow for flexibility for future businesses. 9. The Planning Commission has determined the proposal to modify the hours of delivery in the development will be of benefit to the businesses and the community. 10. Approval of the PD amendment language shall be subject to approval of the Township Attorney. 7 SP #26-009 HTS 8th Amend to PD September 17, 2026 Page 2 Approval is subject to the following conditions: 1. The proposed Amended and Restated Eighth Amendment to Hartland Towne Square Planned Development Agreement is subject to approval by the Township Board. 2. The proposed landscape plan for the roundabout and clock tower areas (Sheet L-C.1) shall be considered a site plan amendment to the previously approved landscape plans for the entire Planned Development and shall not be part of the Amended and Restated Eighth Amendment to Hartland Towne Square Planned Development Agreement. 3. The applicant shall adequately address the outstanding items noted in the Planning Department’s memorandum, September 17, 2026, prior to recording the Planned Development documents. 4. The proposed Amended and Restated Eighth Amendment to Hartland Towne Square Planned Development Agreement shall be in a recordable format and shall comply with the requirements of the Township Attorney. 5. (Any other conditions the Planning Commission deems necessary). Discussion Applicant: Hartland Towne Square LLC Site Description The Hartland Towne Square Planned Development (PD) is located north of Highland Road (M-59) and west of Clark Road in Section 21 of Hartland Township. The entire commercial development is approximately 84.59 acres in size and is comprised of multiple parcels (see Exhibit A – Land). Hartland Towne Square PD is zoned Planned Development (PD) and was approved in 2008. Request The original version of the 8th Amendment to the Hartland Towne Square Planned Development and Pattern Book was submitted as a request to the Township in 2019. The Planning Commission recommended approval of the amendment on August 22, 2019. The Township Board approved the 8th Amendment on September 17, 2019. The 8th Amendment, however, was not recorded. Additional information on the original 8th Amendment is discussed in another section of this memorandum. The new owner of Hartland Towne Square PD, Hartland Towne Square, LLC (“HTS”), is requesting to restate and amend the eighth (8th) amendment to the Hartland Towne Square Planned Development Agreement. The applicant intends to present a document that touches on some of the elements of the original 8th Amendment from 2019 and amend the Planned Development Agreement for other items, adding new language and provisions. The general categories covered in the proposed amendment include internal traffic circulation, on-going road maintenance, drive-through service establishments, signage, uses permitted by right, façade materials, maximum building height, LED lights, and hours of delivery. Additionally, landscape modifications are requested for several existing landscape areas for the selective removal of mature conifer trees which are to be replaced with a juniper shrub species, as outlined in Exhibit G of the PD Amendment. These areas are generally located along the roadside boundaries of an outlot and in common areas. This topic is incorporated into the Amended and Restated Eighth Amendment to Hartland Towne Square Planned Development Agreement. 8 SP #26-009 HTS 8th Amend to PD September 17, 2026 Page 3 A separate aspect of the current application is a request by the applicant to amend the approved landscape plans for Hartland Towne Square for two (2) specific areas. This request is not part of the proposed 8th Amendment to the PD Agreement. The applicant has submitted a proposed landscape plan for the landscape areas associated with the roundabout/traffic circle and clock tower. Modifications are proposed to the current landscape/planting schemes with the removal of some existing plants and the inclusion of new plant materials. The Planning Commission will review the proposed landscape plan as an amendment to the previously approved plans and make a decision. The landscape plan is labeled as sheet L-1.C. Overview and Background Information The Hartland Towne Square Planned Development was approved by the Township on March 18, 2008, under SP #429F. The approved plans for the PD include the Planned Development Agreement (the “Agreement”), the Pattern Book for Hartland Towne Square (site design standards), and the Final Plan (detailed site and landscape plans). Together these documents provide the development standards for Hartland Towne Square PD. Seven (7) amendments to the PD have occurred between 2008 and 2019 as outlined below: 1st Amendment The first amendment to the PD was approved on July 1, 2008. The Agreement, Final Plan (Amended Final Plan, dated June 18, 2008), and Pattern Book (Rev. NO. 3 dated June 18, 2008) were updated in conjunction with the construction of Meijer’s. 2nd Amendment The second amendment to the PD was approved on August 6, 2008, which facilitated the granting of certain alternate access easements within the PD site. The second amendment did not require changes to the previously approved site plans (Amended Final Plan) or Pattern Book. 3rd Amendment On January 20, 2009, the third amendment to the PD Agreement was approved. The text of Paragraph 21 of the PD Agreement (Integration) was amended to establish the required signatories of any amendment to the PD Agreement. Changes to the Amended Final Plan and Pattern Book were not required. 4th Amendment The fourth amendment was approved on March 30, 2009, which amended the text of Paragraph 14.3 of the Agreement as it related to the newly configured Hartland Road and the granting of the Highway Easement to the Livingston County Road Commission. Changes to the Amended Final Plan and Pattern Book were not required. 5th

HOWELL TOWNSHIP PLANNING COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES 3525 Byron Road Howell, MI 48855 August 25, 2026 6:30 P.M. MEMBERS PRESENT: Wayne Williams Matt Stanley Sharon Lollio Tim Boal Trent Holman Cory Alchin Dan Bonello MEMBERS ABSENT: Chair Vice Chair Secretary Board Representative Commissioner Commissioner Commissioner ALSO IN ATTENDANCE: Township Planner Paul Montagno, Applicant Nabil Bazzi, Brent LaVanway with Boss Engineering representing Pineview Village, Patrick Cleary with Boss Engineering representing Soapy Bucket and Zoning Administrator Jonathan Hohenstein Chairman Williams called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm. The roll was called. Chairman Williams requested members rise for the Pledge of Allegiance. APPROVAL OF THE AGENDA: Board Representative Boal suggested adding 12C to allow for data center discussion. Motion by Boal, Second by Lollio, “To approve the agenda as amended.” Motion carried. APPROVAL OF THE MEETING MINUTES: July 28, 2026 Board Representative Boal requested an addition to the minutes specifying what agenda item was deviated to regarding his motion after the violation report, and in the Township Board Report section the word ‘brake’ is misspelled. Motion by Boal, Second by Stanley, “To approve the minutes as amended.” Motion carried. CALL TO THE PUBLIC John Mills, 1750 Oak Grove Rd- Spoke on notifications to adjacent property owners if there is an item on the agenda that shares property lines. ZONING BOARD OF APPEALS REPORT: None TOWNSHIP BOARD REPORT: Draft minutes are included in the packet. Board Representative Boal gave a summary of the meeting. He discussed Michigan Durant LLC. vs Howell Township lawsuit and discussion of an engine brake ordinance. ORDINANCE VIOLATION REPORTS: Report in packet. SCHEDULED PUBLIC HEARINGS: A. PC2026-11: Nabil Bazzi, Request to Rezone Parcel # 4706-21-300-028, Vacant Land, W. Grand River Ave. from Industrial Flex (IFZ) to Neighborhood Service Commercial (NSC)- Township Planner Montagno gave an overview of the request to rezone the property from Industrial Flex (IFZ) to Neighborhood Service Commercial (NSC). The property is 2.2 acres vacant and is located on the South-East corner of Burkhart and Grand River. They are proposing a gas station with a convenience store on the site. Currently in the area is an airport, propane station, commercial and industrial buildings. Neighborhood service zoning is not consistent with the Future Land Use plan or the Master Plan. Board Representative Boal questioned if this was a general rezoning or conditional rezoning. Applicant Nabil Bazzi spoke on his plans for the parcel and answered questions. He is proposing a gas station/oil change and mechanic shop/car wash with food. Board Representative Boal questioned when the property was previously rezoned to Industrial Flex and if they have received any feedback from the Livingston County Road Commission regarding traffic. Chairman Williams questioned how this parcel fits into the Industrial Flex Zoning with large format buildings and only 2.2 acres available. Secretary Lollio questioned if there would be enough business to warrant a gas station and if there would be a food market. Commissioner Bonello questioned if a site plan has been developed. Vice Chair Stanley questioned if that parcel was split from the Hamilton Propane property. Public Hearing was opened by Chairman Williams. Angela Barbash, 4211 Crandall Rd- Spoke in favor of a gas station and Tim Hortons and Wrangler’s Saloon zoning Public Hearing closed by Chairman Williams. Commissioner Holman questioned what other uses would be permitted within a Neighborhood Service Commercial zoning district. Commissioner Alchin questioned if there is a way for the applicant to leave zoning as is but use one of the permitted uses within the Industrial Flex Zone. Secretary Lollio questioned where gas stations fall into the different zoning districts. Commissioner Alchin questioned if there would be an increase in traffic within the Industrial Flex Zone vs Neighborhood Service Commercial zoning. Discussion followed. Motion by Williams, Second by Holman with friendly amendments, “To approve rezoning from Industrial Flex Zone to Neighborhood Service Commercial for Parcel # 4706-21-300-028. This decision is based upon the neighboring property that is a current Neighborhood Service Commercial zoning and that the size of this particular parcel has limited accommodations for industrial, medium, or heavy commercial use. Amending that the property referenced is in the same quadrant as RSC and not NSC. Motion carried. OTHER MATTERS TO BE REVIEWED BY THE PLANNING COMMISSION: A. MSU Extension-Discretionary Standards Common to Special Land Use Case Law- Satkowiak v. Township of Beaver- Discussion followed. OLD BUSINESS: None NEW BUSINESS: 1. PC2026-08: Pineview Village Phase II, JMF Brewer LLC, 4706-27-200-014, Preliminary Site Plan ReviewPlanner Montagno reviewed the site plan for a multi-unit development with six townhome buildings that contain 4 units each for a total of 24 units each with two bedrooms. This is north of the existing development in that area; there are 68 existing homes that have been developed on a private drive. The development would not have impact on the existing wetlands. They have proposed a boundary adjustment with the adjacent property to the north that they currently own. They provide two parking spots with garages on each unit. Driveways will be 20 feet long with sidewalk on one side of the proposed drive which is consistent with the existing development, and they are also requesting a waiver for landscape requirements along Brewer Road. Commissioner Bonello questioned patio placement. Chairman Williams questioned the Township Planner’s reasoning for the property line adjustment recommendation. Applicant Brent LaVanway from Boss Engineering spoke on the project and answered questions. They are preserving open space in the east portion that backs up to Brewer Road and wetlands will not be impacted. There will be a minor road extension coming off to the west to accommodate the three westerly buildings. Chairman Williams questioned the lighting plan. Commissioner Bonello questioned if the homeowners could control the lights. Board Representative Boal questioned if problems with the grinder pumps and the sewers have been resolved and if they had any concerns complying with the letters from MHOG, Engineer, and Drain Commissioner, if anything is planned with the property to the north and there is also no proposed landscaping planned on the east side of the building only pre-existing natural landscaping. Discussion followed. Motion by Boal, Second by Stanley with friendly amendments “To conditionally approve the preliminary site plan PC2026-08: Pineview Village Phase II subject to the compliance with the Drain Commissioner, MHOG, Township engineers, and any outstanding issues in the Township Planner’s report with the exception of the setbacks, property line adjustments, and the fire reports. So, with the exception of not landscaping the east side of the property.” Motion carried. 2. PC2026-09: Soapy Bucket, Russell Springborn, 4706-25-200-048, Amendments to approved site planPlanner Montagno gave an overview of the request. Applicant is requesting an amendment to the site plan to construct the car wash in phases. Phase 1 would address the road, utilities and temporary detention pond. Phase 2 would be the construction of the pump station, and Phase 3 is the building that will house the detail shop, RV wash and parking. Phase 3A and 3B would be the lighting, landscaping, permanent pond and car wash building. They are not planning on occupying the buildings until all phases are complete. Chairman Williams questioned if this was the original project approved just broken up in phases but no major structural changes. Board Commissioner Boal clarified that the applicant needed to return to the Planning Commission for approval of the phasing plan, as the preliminary site plan was previously approved three years ago. Engineer Patrick Cleary with Boss Engineering and owner Russell Springborn discussed the reasoning behind the phasing and answered questions. Chairman Williams questioned if there was a timeline from breaking ground to washing cars. Commissioner Bonello questioned how long the pauses would be between phases. Secretary Lollio questioned how it was decided in what would encompass each phase. Board Representative Boal questioned if the concept for a car wash is still feasible since it has been three years since original approval, temporary detention plan and if there are any plans to develop the other property to the north in the future. Motion by Stanley, Second by Alchin, with friendly amendments “For PC2026-09 Soapy Bucket Property # 4706-25-200-048 to amend the site plan to allow for the phasing with an updated site plan laying out all the phasing with the final site plan shall be submitted for each phase according to section 20.12 and however no part of phase 3A or 3B shall be occupied until the entire phase is complete. We’ll amend the motion to include the approval of the final site plan 1 and subject to the approval of the Township engineer.” Motion carried. 3. Data Center Discussion- Resident Research Committee member Kristin Dennison spoke on PUE vs TUE which is the power use effectiveness metric vs the total use effectiveness metric. Commissioner Alchin questioned how to track statistics and information appropriate for a Township of our size. Board Representative Boal gave an update on the next subcommittee meeting, MTA provided sample Data Center ordinance, the County Board of Commissioners approved a resolution for a county wide sound ordinance and newsletter from Bethel Suites regarding affordable housing. Planner Montagno answered questions. CALL TO THE PUBLIC: Denie Perkola, 3460 Mason Rd- Spoke on outdated Township masterplan ADJOURNMENT: Motion by Boal, Second by Holman, “To adjourn.” Motion carried. Howell, MI 48855 September 14, 2026 6:30 P.M. MEMBERS PRESENT: Robert Spaulding Sue Daus Jonathan Hohenstein Matthew Counts Tim Boal Jodi Fulton Bob Wilson MEMBERS ABSENT: Supervisor Clerk Treasurer Trustee Trustee Trustee Trustee Also in Attendance: 12 people signed in Eileen Zilch with Community Catalysts Supervisor Spaulding called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. The roll was called. McCririe v. Howell Township Treasurer Hohenstein reported that the court documents for McCririe v. Howell Township were included in the packet for the Board’s review. B. Michigan Durant v. Howell Township Treasurer Hohenstein reported that the court documents for Michigan Durant v. Howell Township were included in the packet for the Board’s review. C. Engine Brake Ordinance – Discussion The Board discussed engine/jake braking concerns, potential use of state grant funds for Sheriff’s traffic enforcement, and options for enforcement through the Township’s existing nuisance ordinance. Motion by Fulton, Second by Hohenstein, “To table the discussion on jake brake ordinance and signage pending information from the Sherrif’s department on enforceability.” Motion carried. Community Catalysts – Bethel Homes Project Information Community Catalysts representative Eileen Zilch discussed how a community land trust would work in connection with the Bethel Homes project to make homeownership more affordable. Huron Cemetery Maintenance Contract Clerk Daus reviewed the proposed three-year cemetery agreement and the updated fees compared with the Township’s current contract. Board discussion on the timing and cost of the proposed update, coordination with the ongoing zoning ordinance rewrite. The Board also discussed the need to establish priorities and a timeline for the various planning projects. Motion by Counts, Second by Boal, “To table new business item 8-C, Township Master Plan Update Proposal, pending budget information as well as planner information on timeline.” Motion carried CALL TO THE PUBLIC: Charles Smith, 5136 Fleming Rd.: Spoke on voting rights, citizenship, EPA, and data centers concerns Todd Kozakiewicz, 6205 Raddatz Rd.: Spoke on the Resident Research Committee, Saline data center 2 9-14-2026 Debbie Mannisto, 2330 Tooley Rd.: Spoke on the Bethel Homes Project Denie Perkola, 3460 Mason Rd.: Spoke on the Township Master Plan REPORTS: A. SUPERVISOR: Supervisor Spaulding sought the Board’s guidance on the possibility of holding a joint meeting of the Township Board, Planning Commission, and ZBA to discuss and prioritize key community needs, including roads, budgets, parks, and the Master Plan. He also reminded residents to sign up for email notifications on the Township website to stay informed about topics and issues of interest. B. TREASURER: Jonathan noted that it was an exceptionally busy tax day and thanked Marie and Teresa for ensuring the collection process ran smoothly. C. CLERK: Clerk Daus reported that new cemetery signs have been installed to replace the old plywood structures on Fleming Road and Burkhart Road. Additionally, she reported that preparations are underway for the November election. D. ZONING: See Zoning Administrator Hohenstein’s report E. ASSESSING: See Assessor Kilpela’s report F. FIRE AUTHORITY: See report G. MHOG: Trustee Counts reported that the cross-country main and sanatorium project is expected to wrap up in October. Recent utility maintenance included cleaning the Hometown tower and performing an emergency repair on Wellhead 2. Additionally, he reported that the 2027 budget was approved, which incorporates a minimal rate increase of under $3.00 per quarter. H. PLANNING COMMISSION: Trustee Boal reported that a public hearing was held regarding a rezoning request for a 2.2-acre parcel at the intersection of Burkhart Road and Grand River Avenue. The Board approved preliminary site plans for an expansion at Pineview Village as well as a phased construction plan for Soapy Bucket Car Wash. Additionally, he reported that the Data Center Subcommittee, with input from the Resident Research Committee (RRC), completed its final draft ordinance to submit to the Township Planner. Following Planning Commission review and legal vetting, a public hearing will be scheduled. I. ZONING BOARD OF APPEALS (ZBA): No report 3 9-14-2026 J. WWTP: Treasurer Hohenstein reported that utility operators neutralized a cyber-attack on water plant controllers by switching to manual mode and applying a software patch. Water safety and service remained unaffected. The Township Supervisor is the moderator of the meeting. In the absence of the Supervisor, the Township Clerk shall hold an election of the Board Members present to select a moderator for the meeting. Anyone attending the meeting either in-person or on-line may speak during the “Call to the Public” part of the meeting. To preserve order, those attending in- person will speak first. When all in-person attendees have been heard, the moderator will ask if any on-line attendee wishes to speak. When recognized by the moderator, in-person attendees shall come to the podium. The moderator will request that they give their name and address before they begin their comments. When all in-person attendees have finished speaking, the moderator will ask if anyone attending the meeting on-line wishes to speak. On-line attendees may unmute themselves and when recognized by the moderator may speak. On-line attendees will also be asked for their name and address. All comments shall be addressed to the Township Board. The “Call to the Public” is for attendees to provide information or opinions to the Township Board and is not intended to be a dialog. Anyone needing a response should contact officials or staff during working hours. To preserve efficiency, speakers will be asked to keep their comments to three minutes or less. After evaluating the dimensional standards of neighboring communities, it became evident that the township's current provisions are more stringent. As a result, the Commission reached a consensus to revise standards to be more permissive, including lot coverage and setbacks, for both the Highway Services District and the Industrial Service Districts. These revisions are intended to allow more efficient land use while still preventing intensive uses from encroaching on nearby residential zoning districts. The Commission also noted that the limited number of parcels within the Industrial District may inadvertently constrain industrial development. To avoid the Township being perceived as excluding industrial uses, the next Master Plan update should include substantial public engagement to help identify appropriate areas for future industrial uses. A comparative table of dimensional standards from surrounding communities has been included to support discussion of the proposed amendments. Considerations and Discussion 1. How do these standards impact adjacent properties now and into the future? 2. Do the revisions meet the intent of the Zoning District? 3. Are the amendments consistent with the Master Plan’s future land use designations of Commercial and Industrial? Grand River Ave. Suite 206 • (517) 546-7555 Fax (517) 552-2347 • Web Site Milivcounty.com/planning TO: Marion Township Planning Commission FROM: Martha Haglund, AICP, Principal Planner DATE: September 11, 2026 SUBJECT: DRAFT 17.36 Data Center Ordinance At the July 23, 2026, Township Board Meeting the moratorium on Hyper Scale Data Centers was extended an additional 6 months from the original expiration date of August 13, 2026, and will now expire on February 11, 2027. This extension will provide the necessary time to finalize a Data Center Ordinance. To date, Marion Township has not received an application to develop a data center in the Township. During the Township Planning Commission meeting on August 25, 2026, the draft Data Center Ordinance was reviewed, alongside discussions regarding potential locations for permitting data centers. There was a consensus to allow data centers within the Light Industrial and Highway Service Commercial zoning districts. Additionally, amendments to the dimensional standards for these districts were proposed to allow more efficiency land use while preventing encroachment on residential zoning districts. In conjunction with the revisions to the zoning districts, several changes to the draft Data Center Ordinance were proposed to ensure feasibility for development. This is important to ensure that the Township does not appear exclusionary toward specific land uses, which could expose it to legal risks. Notably, the setback requirement from residential zoning districts was reduced from 500 feet to 250 feet, while maintaining buffer provisions to mitigate impacts on neighboring properties. Additionally, there is a 2-acre minimum, down from the previous 10-acre minimum lot size. Other revisions from the previous draft include: • Permitting battery storage to support on-site renewable energy generation. • Introducing standards for generator emissions. • Discussion on sound regulations. • Mandating documentation from the wastewater treatment facility regarding capacity and water filtration capabilities. • Requiring the power usage agreement to specify a maximum level of consumption; should the project seek to exceed this limit, Township Board approval will be necessary. • Removing the violation section. text: CHARTER TOWNSHIP OF OXFORD PLANNING COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 A regular meeting of the Charter Township of Oxford Planning Commission was held Thursday, September 10, 2026, at the Oxford High School Performing Arts Center, 745 N. Oxford Road, Oxford, Michigan 48371. 1. CALL TO ORDER The meeting was called to order by Chair Bailey at 6:30 p.m. 2. RESPECTS TO THE FLAG 3. ROLL CALL Members Present: Patti Durr, Ryan Austin, Robert Turner, Mark Blankenship, David Wagner, Korey Bailey Members Absent: Don Wloszek (excused) Also Present: Township Planner Matteo Passalacqua, Township Planner Benny Bono, Township Attorney Zack Learman, Township Engineer Jim Sharpe, Building Official Tim London, Planning and Zoning Coordinator Debra Walton, Deputy Supervisor Danielle Smith, Recording Secretary Susan McCullough, one OCTV camera operator, and approximately 350 attendees. 4. APPROVAL OF AGENDA Commissioner Wagner moved, Commissioner Turner seconded, to approve the Charter Township of Oxford regular Planning Commission agenda for Thursday, September 10, 2026 as presented. Ayes: 6 Nays: 0 Absent: 1 Motion Carried. 5. CONFLICTS OF INTEREST/EX-PARTE CONTACT None. 6. APPROVAL OF MINUTES Planning Commission Regular Meeting – August 27, 2026 Commissioner Wagner moved, Commissioner Blankenship seconded, to approve the minutes of the regular Planning Commission meeting for August 27, 2026 as presented. Ayes: 6 Nays: 0 Absent: 1 Motion Carried. 7. PUBLIC COMMENT Public comment began at 6:40 p.m. One person spoke during public comment. Public comment ended at 6:41 p.m. Page 1 – Charter Township of Oxford Planning Commission Minutes CHARTER TOWNSHIP OF OXFORD PLANNING COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 8. PUBLIC HEARING(S) A. Zoning Ordinance Text Amendments to update Article 2, Section 2.2, of the Township of Oxford Zoning Ordinance, is to establish a definition of “Data Center” and provide regulations for large-scale data processing, computer server, data storage, telecommunications equipment, and associated infrastructure uses. These facilities are used for the processing, storage, and transmission of digital information and may include supporting infrastructure such as backup power generation, cooling systems, fuel storage, and security systems. The proposed amendments to Article 10, Section 10.1.J and 10.1.K, to modify noise and vibration standards for all uses in the Township. These standards will be applicable to data centers as well as all other uses in the Township. The proposed amendments to Article 3, Section 3.5, to make data centers a special land use in the Data Center Overlay District. This overlay has been applied to Light Industrial (I-1) and General Industrial (I-2) zoned parcels north of Ray Road and south of Davison Lake Road. The proposed addition to Article 5, Section 5.41. This section addresses required noise studies, cooling system design, anticipated utility demand and capacity verification, traffic analysis, screening and sound barrier standards, security measures, backup power generation and fuel storage, and decommissioning plans. B. Consideration of a Zoning Map Amendment to establish a Data Center Overlay District on all properties zoned Light Industrial (I-1) and General Industrial (I-2) located north of Ray Road and south of Davison Lake Road. The purpose of the proposed Data Center Overlay district would be to allow data centers as a special land use on those parcels. Chair Bailey reviewed the order of the proceedings. Presentation by the Petitioner The petition was presented by Matteo Passalacqua, Carlisle|Wortman Associates, Inc., 117 North First Street, Suite 70, Ann Arbor, MI. Comments from Township Consultants and Staff Township Planner Passalacqua presented the proposed changes and was available to answer any questions of the Commission. The proposed engineering report requirements from Township Engineer Sharpe were included in the Commission packet and he was available to answer any questions of the Commission. The proposed Data Center and Life Safety Review Requirements from the Oxford Fire Department was included in the Commission packet. Open Public Hearing Commissioner Wagner moved, Commissioner Austin seconded, to open the public hearing at 7:26 p.m. Ayes: 6 Nays: 0 Absent: 1 Motion Carried. Page 2 – Charter Township of Oxford Planning Commission Minutes CHARTER TOWNSHIP OF OXFORD PLANNING COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 State Representative Josh Schriver, 597 Mechanic Street, Oxford MI, thanked the Planning Commission and the Township for being proactive regarding the regulation of data centers. He urged the Planning Commission to take the time to adopt reasonable regulations prior to the expiration of the moratorium. State Representative Donni Steele, 742 Lawson, Orion MI, thanked Planner Passalacqua for his presentation and explanation. She also thanked the Planning Commission for their service and the public for coming to the meeting. Bruce Downey, 1346 Meadowbrook Ct., Oxford MI, appreciated the presentation and expressed concern with the proposed decibel levels, water consumption, electricity consumption, screening requirements, and damage to roads during construction. Linda Van Houten, 2253 Shipman Rd., Oxford MI, expressed concern with water and electricity consumption, effects on the value of homes and effects on wildlife. Mikayla Casolari, 285 Stony Lake Dr., Oxford MI, mentioned notification to all residents, would like to see a demonstrated need for a data center in Oxford and concerns with security measures. Ed Rumsas, 457 Southshore Dr., Oxford MI, expressed concern with setbacks and would like to see a requirement for berms. He is also concerned with electrical consumption and the effect on the infrastructure, water consumption and sound issues. He would like to see additional training for fire, police and other emergency services at the developer’s expense, as well as a decommission plan and bond requirement. Jennifer Gudgel, 1490 Glass Lake Cir., Oxford MI, expressed concern with the sound pollution especially as it travels over water. Mike Ratajski, 235 Stony Lake Dr., Oxford MI, is opposed to the site overlay. He would like to see the Township character maintained and expressed concern with noise and health impacts. Breaha Wallin, 240 N. Hurd Rd., Ortonville MI appreciates the township’s proactive approach and expressed concern with health impacts. She requested a size limitation and expressed concern with enforcement, penalties for violation of restrictions, generator use and a restriction on the timing of their use. Melissa Haynes, 95 Brabb Rd., Oxford MI expressed concern with protecting the lakes and the infrastructure requirements. She urged protection of the community. David Preuss, 1400 Glass Lake Cir., Oxford MI would like to see the rural character maintained. He suggested Oxford Township learn from other communities and expressed concern with decibel levels, setbacks, and water consumption. Bruce Williams, 741 W. Bay Shore Dr., Oxford MI suggested that the sound levels be adjusted, with tonal penalties. He thanked Planner Passalacqua for his presentation. He is also concerned with light pollution and suggested that the community vote on whether to allow data centers. He is concerned with water consumption, unauthorized expansion, and would like to see performance (surety) bond requirements expanded. Michael Calin, 5820 Hempstead Rd., Metamora MI asked about the cost of all the studies and whether the developer funds the reviews and studies by the professionals. He expressed environmental concerns, and suggested land purchases be monitored. Page 3 – Charter Township of Oxford Planning Commission Minutes CHARTER TOWNSHIP OF OXFORD PLANNING COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 Ned Wroblewski-Zimmer, 611 Bay Pointe Dr., Oxford MI, stated that he appreciated the presentation. He expressed concern with water consumption and suggested the burden of proof should lie with the developer. He would like to see the words “may” be replaced with “shall” in the proposed language.
